sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Immunoprecipitation with anti-HA antibody after E. coli incubation confirmed surface expression; construct explicitly stated to be fully functional equivalent to wild-type MR1 (L2/L3).
sites.rationale: MR1 has exactly one extracellular terminus: the mature N-terminus at residue 23, exposed after cleavage of the 22-residue signal peptide. Because the ledger names no insertion residue, the junction is topology-derived at insert_after_residue=22 (residue S22 → R23), placing the tag 278 residues from the TM boundary. Python verification confirms S at position 22 and R at position 23. The anti-HA surface IP on intact cells (L3) and explicit functional equivalence statement (L2) together support surface_and_function validation. HA-tagged MR1 stably expressed in Thp1 cells (Thp1.MR1.HA); the ledger clips (L1–L3) name the construct but do not state the insertion residue. MR1 is a type I transmembrane protein with a single extracellular terminus: the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 23 (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 22). The anti-HA immunoprecipitation performed on intact cells after overnight E. coli incubation (L3) demonstrates that the HA epitope is surface-accessible, consistent with placement immediately after the signal-peptide cleavage site. The construct is confirmed fully functional equivalent to wild-type MR1 (L2).

sources.claim: Thp1 and Thp1.MR1.HA cells were incubated overnight with fixed E. coli and MR1 was immunoprecipitated using an antibody directed against the HA tag.

literature_notes: L4–L10 all describe MR1-GFP constructs. The consistent 'MR1-GFP' nomenclature (protein name first, then GFP) denotes a C-terminal fusion; MR1's C-terminus (residues 324–341) is intracellular per the topology landmarks. These constructs therefore carry GFP on the cytoplasmic face and do not qualify as extracellular surface-tag sites. They are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line reports an insertion in any internal extracellular loop of MR1, so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: MR1-GFP fusion (C-terminal GFP) expressed in HeLa and C1R cells; MR1's C-terminus (residues 324–341) is intracellular, so GFP resides on the cytoplasmic face and is not a surface tag.
Doxycycline-inducible TET-MR1GFP construct in BEAS-2B cells; same C-terminal GFP fusion, intracellular face confirmed by topology.
